page: Amazon Web Services m9g.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by a single-core AWS Graviton processor. Built on the ARMv9 architecture with Neoverse-V3 cores, this instance features 1 dedicated physical core running at 3.3 GHz with 1 thread per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance alongside clear multi-threaded and resource-density limitations. The m9g.medium achieves top-tier results in single-threaded tasks, as evidenced by its Geekbench single-core score of 2239.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 36.08 GB/sec. However, because it is constrained to a single vCPU, its multi-core performance is poor, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1988.18 and a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2235.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are mixed; while large-block read-only bandwidth is average at 43.27 GB/sec, small-block cached reads and large-block writes are poor, registering at 136.49 GB/sec and 13.7 GB/sec respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the Graviton9 ARM ecosystem, providing dedicated CPU allocation without the burstable credit constraints of shared-core instances. However, the single-core configuration presents significant tradeoffs, resulting in weak performance for parallelized workloads such as software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, simple background scripts, and minor utility workloads that do not require high multi-threaded throughput or local storage.
